content: Oxiconazole is an antifungal medication prescribed to treat skin infections such as athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm. It may also be used for other conditions as determined by your doctor. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Oxiconazole is available as a cream or lotion and is applied directly to the skin. It is typically used once daily in the evening or twice daily, in the morning and evening. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use oxiconazole exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than prescribed. Before application, clean the affected area thoroughly, allow it to dry, and then gently rub the medication into the skin until most of it disappears. Use only enough medication to cover the affected area. Wash your hands after applying the medication. Before using oxiconazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to oxiconazole or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using oxiconazole, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Oxiconazole may cause mild side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: itching, burning, redness, dry or flaky skin, or tingling. Serious side effects are rare but may include pain, swelling, open sores, or a skin rash. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store oxiconazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Oxiconazole is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of oxiconazole, contact your doctor.
